back: One sample of light intensity per channel at a grid location; not an area.
HWC $(H,W,C)$: files, PIL, OpenCV. CHW $(C,H,W)$: PyTorch. Convert with transpose(2,0,1).
uint8 0..255 (files), float 0..1 (divide by 255), standardised (subtract channel mean, divide by channel std).
Mean and std have shape (3,) and broadcast over the LAST axis in HWC.
HSV: separate hue from brightness for colour thresholding. YCbCr: brightness vs colour differences, used by JPEG and video.
Nearest: labels/masks. Bilinear: default for training. Bicubic/Lanczos: sharper, for viewing.
$[[-1,0,1],[-2,0,2],[-1,0,1]]$: right minus left, middle row doubled; responds to vertical edges. $G=\sqrt{G_x^2+G_y^2}$.
$\frac19\mathbf 1_{3\times3}$: local mean; reduces noise, softens edges.
Counts of pixels per brightness bin; ignores location; reveals under-exposure or clipping.
Must preserve the label; apply to training images only. Examples: flip, reflect-padded crop, colour jitter, mixup.
uint8 into a float model, BGR vs RGB, wrong layout, missing or wrong mean/std, different resize than training.
